question: Where did the gene version that helps Tibetans thrive at high altitude come from?
answer: From Denisovans, an extinct group of ancient humans. Huerta-Sánchez and colleagues found the Tibetan version of the EPAS1 gene, which keeps blood from thickening dangerously in thin air, almost identical to one in a Denisovan genome. It entered modern humans through interbreeding tens of thousands of years ago, then spread on the plateau.
move: Some of your best assets were borrowed long ago from someone else.
ask: Which strength of mine did I inherit or borrow from someone I rarely credit?
reference: Huerta-Sánchez et al., Altitude adaptation in Tibetans caused by introgression of Denisovan-like DNA, Nature, 2014
